commitResults.messageBody:
The starter project uses the Duke name and branding.

Rename the entry point and documentation to Groot, and replace the
banner to give the chatbot a consistent identity.

The chatbot only displays its banner and does not address the user.

Add a greeting, prompt, separators, and farewell to give each session a
clear beginning and end.

The chatbot exits immediately after greeting the user.

Read and echo commands until the user enters `bye` so a session can
support continuous interaction.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add in-memory task storage and listing
commitResults.messageBody:
Echoed commands are not retained, so users cannot review earlier input.

Store task descriptions in memory and add the `list` command to display
them in insertion order.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command to mark tasks as done
commitResults.messageBody:
Stored tasks do not record whether they have been completed.

Track completion state and add the `mark` command so users can update
and view a task status. Ignore generated Java build output as well.

Users can mark a task as done but cannot correct that status later.

Add the `unmark` command so a completed task can be returned to its
pending state.

commitResults.messageTitle: Encapsulate task state in Task class
commitResults.messageBody:
Task descriptions and completion flags are stored in parallel arrays,
which can become inconsistent as task behavior grows.

Introduce a Task class that owns its description, completion state,
status updates, and display format. Store Task objects in one array.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add todo, deadline, and event task types
commitResults.messageBody:
All tasks share one generic representation, so dated tasks lose their
meaning and display details.

Add Todo, Deadline, and Event subclasses and parse their respective
input formats. Record UI tests to verify polymorphic storage and status
updates.

Malformed commands can terminate the chatbot or corrupt task state.

Validate task details and task numbers, and report input problems
through a dedicated GrootException without ending the session. Add UI
coverage for invalid commands and confirm rejected input does not alter
stored tasks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add task deletion with dynamic storage
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks are stored in a fixed-size array, which complicates deletion and
capacity management.

Use an ArrayList to manage tasks. Add the `delete` command so users can
remove tasks by number, validate deletion input, and report the updated
task count.

Update the documentation and UI tests to cover task reindexing, retained
status, invalid input, and deletion from an empty list.

Command keywords are repeated as strings throughout parsing, which makes
the supported command set difficult to manage consistently.

Introduce CommandType to centralize keywords and argument rules.
Dispatch commands through the enum so invalid inputs remain distinct
from supported commands.

Extend UI tests with command boundary cases. Prevent invalid list or bye
arguments from changing or ending the session.

The README does not explain how AI tools contributed to the project.

Add an AI use section that records Codex's role in design,
implementation, testing, documentation, and Git maintenance. Clarify
that suggestions were reviewed and verified using Java 25 UI tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add file persistence for task list
commitResults.messageBody: Save task changes automatically and restore all task types and completion states at startup. Extend UI coverage with an isolated restart scenario to verify the saved data round trip.

commitResults.messageTitle: Harden task persistence against data errors
commitResults.messageBody: Validate stored records, escape structural characters, and report read or write failures without stack traces. Save through atomic replacement and roll back in-memory mutations when persistence fails so disk and memory remain consistent.
Build and display the data path through java.nio.file.Path so separators remain platform dependent. Document and verify first-run behavior when both the data directory and task file are absent.

Validate deadline input as ISO yyyy-MM-dd, store it as LocalDate, and present dates in a readable English format. Preserve ISO dates through file storage and extend UI coverage for leap days, invalid dates, and restart loading.

Move command recognition, task construction, deadline validation, and task-index parsing into a dedicated Parser class. Keep Groot focused on application flow and task mutations while preserving every existing console response and persistence behavior.

Move collection ownership and task mutations behind a dedicated TaskList API. Give persistence an immutable snapshot and preserve explicit rollback operations so failed saves cannot leave the in-memory list inconsistent.

Group parsing, storage, exceptions, and task models by responsibility while retaining src/main/java as the source root. Update setup documentation and the AI-use declaration to reflect the new layout.
Point the application plugin at the packaged groot.Groot entry point so Gradle run starts this chatbot instead of the upstream template class.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for command recognition
commitResults.messageBody: Cover exact keywords, argument acceptance, argumentless commands, keyword boundaries, unknown input, and case sensitivity so parser command classification regressions are caught early.
Add whitespace and command-boundary cases for the highest-value CommandType logic. Document the approximately 50 percent high-value method target and require JUnit review after each code change.
Name the Shadow artifact groot.jar and explicitly set its packaged main class so it runs with java -jar. Document how to build, locate, and launch the artifact on supported platforms.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align Java code with SE-EDU conventions
commitResults.messageBody:
Switch layout and collection naming do not fully match the project
coding standard, which makes the style inconsistent.

Indent switch cases, mark intentional fallthroughs, separate logical
blocks, use plural collection names, and adopt American spelling.

These changes improve consistency without changing runtime behavior.

Java changes need a consistent project-specific style reference that
agents can apply before handing work back.

Add a tracked skill based on the SE-EDU intermediate Java standard and
mandate it in the project agent instructions. Update the AI declaration
to record the assistance.

Commit preparation needs consistent message and branch conventions in
addition to the repository's authorization safeguards.

Add a tracked skill based on the SE-EDU Git guide and require agents to
apply it to future commit work. Preserve the rule that commits and
pushes require explicit user permission.

Users need a quick way to locate tasks without scanning the full list.

Add case-insensitive description matching through the find command while
preserving task order and list state. Cover parsing, matching, invalid
input, and UI output with JUnit and console tests.

Public APIs need consistent documentation for readers and maintainers.

Document public classes, constructors, methods, enum constants, exposed
fields, and test methods. Preserve existing documentation for non-trivial
storage helpers, and record the assistance in the AI-use declaration.

The Javadoc branch documents the project public APIs.

Merge the branch without fast-forwarding so its independent history and
branch boundary remain visible.

The coding-standard branch contains the Java cleanup and the tracked
Java and Git agent skills.

Merge the branch without fast-forwarding so its independent commits and
branch boundary remain visible.

Integrate case-insensitive task-description search together with its
parser, JUnit, console UI, and user documentation coverage.

Keep the merge explicit so the Level-9 branch remains visible as a third
parallel increment.

# Conflicts:
#	src/main/java/groot/Groot.java
#	src/main/java/groot/parser/CommandType.java

Project-specific skills need to remain available in the local workspace
without becoming part of the repository history.

Remove their ignore exceptions, stop tracking the existing copies, and
keep the local files ignored.

Cover searches that have no matching task description.

Use an explicit void-compatible lambda for the missing-keyword
assertion.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document AI assistance for find tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Record Codex's role in resolving the JUnit warning and extending
find test coverage.

Keep the declaration accurate and transparent about AI use.

commitResults.messageTitle: Enforce SE-EDU style in Gradle builds

commitResults.messageBody: Reuse Groot's command-processing path from both console and JavaFX interfaces. Package the tutorial layouts, styles, images, and JavaFX runtime dependencies in the executable JAR.
Integrate the JavaFX graphical interface while preserving the existing console command path.

Allow command types to declare a canonical keyword and optional aliases
through varargs. Add common help aliases and provide a direct-task
TaskList constructor for concise setup.

Document the supported commands and extend automated coverage for the new
calling forms.

Integrate varargs-backed command aliases and direct task-list
construction.

Command dispatch and task status changes depend on contracts that
ordinary input validation cannot verify. Broken internal contracts
can otherwise remain hidden during development.

Add assertions for recognized commands, non-negative task counts,
and expected completion states. Explain each assumption and keep
user-input validation separate so normal errors remain recoverable.

Enable assertions in JUnit and document how to enable them when
running the application. Cover invalid input and faulty task
subclasses to distinguish user mistakes from programming errors.

commitResults.messageTitle: Separate task parsing by task type
commitResults.messageBody:
Task creation combines three command formats and their validation
in one method. Readers must follow unrelated branches and interpret
hard-coded offsets to understand each format.

Delegate task creation to a focused parser for each task type and
name the command markers. Keep each method at one level of
abstraction so validation rules are easier to read and maintain.

Preserve accepted formats and existing error messages. Add parser
tests and interleaved valid and invalid console inputs to guard
against accidental changes in behavior or task state.

Command dispatch mixes routing, mutation, saving, and response
formatting. Mark and unmark repeat the same recovery logic, making
future changes harder to review and keep consistent.

Delegate commands to focused handlers and share the status-update
path. Keep command routing short while retaining the existing
responses and restoring task state when saving fails.

Add isolated tests for failed saves, repeated status changes, and
restoration of deleted tasks. Extend console coverage to check
invalid indices between successful commands.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use streams for command and alias lookup
commitResults.messageBody:
Command recognition searches command types and aliases with
explicit loops. Both searches express matching queries rather than
changes to application state.

Express these queries with streams while retaining the first
matching command and the unknown-command fallback. Preserve alias
handling, argument boundaries, and short-circuit behavior so the
refactoring does not broaden the accepted command syntax.

Extend command and console tests for keywords inside arguments,
alias prefixes, and rejected input that must leave tasks unchanged.

The assertions branch documents internal contracts that are not
yet checked on master. Integrating it makes those development-time
checks available without replacing normal user-input validation.

Merge PR #1 with an explicit merge commit to preserve the feature
branch history. Include the assertion rationale, execution guidance,
and regression tests alongside the production checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Integrate assertions into the code-quality branch
commitResults.messageBody:
Master contains the assertions milestone, while the code-quality
branch changes the same dispatcher and adds overlapping tests.
The conflicts prevent PR #2 from being merged safely.

Integrate master and resolve the conflicts by retaining the focused
command handlers together with the dispatcher assertion. Combine
the regression tests so neither branch loses its coverage.

Keep assertions enabled in child test processes and preserve the
console cases for invalid input and repeated status changes.
Verify the combined behavior before merging the feature into master.

Task parsing and command dispatch on master combine multiple
responsibilities. The code-quality branch separates those concerns
and removes duplicated status-update recovery logic.

Merge PR #2 after integrating the assertions changes and resolving
the overlapping code and tests. Preserve existing command syntax,
responses, and failed-save recovery behavior.

Use an explicit merge commit to retain the feature branch history
and distinguish the refactoring from its integration into master.

commitResults.messageTitle: Integrate master into the Streams branch
commitResults.messageBody:
The Streams branch predates the assertions and code-quality work
now on master. Its isolated checks do not establish that all three
features work together.

Merge master into the branch before accepting PR #3. Retain the
stream-based lookup alongside the assertions, focused command
handlers, and combined regression tests.

Verify the integrated code with JUnit, console tests with assertions
enabled, and style checks on Java 25. Preserve the merge history
without introducing unrelated behavior changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge stream-based command lookup into master
commitResults.messageBody:
The Streams branch expresses command and alias lookup as matching
queries while preserving the existing recognition rules. It has
also been verified with the assertions and code-quality changes.

Merge PR #3 to bring that refactoring into master. Keep the existing
command syntax, alias behavior, and unknown-command responses.

Preserve the feature and integration history with an explicit merge
commit rather than squashing or rebasing the branch.

Build and style checks depend on developers running them locally.
A successful local build alone may miss platform-specific failures.

Add a workflow based on the SE-EDU template to check pushes and pull
requests on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Use Java 25 with JavaFX to
match the project's runtime requirements.

Validate the Gradle wrapper, run tests and style checks, and build
the packaged application. Limit repository permissions to read-only
access and document local verification and authentication setup.

The CI branch adds automated validation that is not yet available
on master. Integrating it gives future changes consistent build,
test, style, and packaging checks across three operating systems.

Merge branch-A-CI with an explicit merge commit so the workflow
change remains distinct from its integration. Keep the A-CI tag on
this integration point to identify the completed milestone.

Include setup instructions and local verification guidance so
developers can reproduce the checks before pushing changes.

Deadlines appear in main-list order, making due dates difficult to
compare. Reordering stored tasks would also change the task numbers
used by existing commands.

Add an earliest-first deadline display with optional reverse flags.
Keep original task numbers and saved order unchanged so users can
act on displayed tasks without changing how the main list behaves.

Keep equal-date descriptions alphabetical in both directions and
accept case and whitespace variations only for sort. Document these
rules and test ordering, validation, selection, and persistence with
JUnit and recorded console cases.

The C-Sort branch provides chronological deadline views without
changing the stored task order. Its tests protect task selection
and persistence as well as the new command's validation rules.

Merge PR #4 after the Linux, macOS, and Windows checks pass. Preserve
the feature history with an explicit merge commit and retain C-Sort
as the tag for this integration point.

Keep sorting display-only and leave event handling, other command
syntax, and the storage format unchanged.
